clue.text: Start embracing R Haggard

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within your arms, so the first word wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: the dawn is the start of the day
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reads like a note that the novelist H. Rider Haggard is being welcomed at the start of something.
explanation.walkthrough: R Haggard looks like the author's name; Haggard is the definition, an adjective, and R is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drawn looks tired and strained in the face, which is exactly what haggard describes.

clue.text: Diamonds I guess I'd mistakenly concealed

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the preceding letters are set down in the wrong order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to wrongly guessing that some jewels had been hidden away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disguised has had its true appearance covered up, so it is hidden from view.

clue.text: Admit a sin, scratching bottom

indicators.note: to scratch something is to strike it off, and the bottom of a down entry is its last letter, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A confession scene in which someone owns up to a sin while scratching their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The sin is greed; dropping its last letter leaves GREE after A, giving AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit a point in argument is to concede or accept it, the same as going along with it.

clue.text: Grandmother eager for fabric

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
keen means eager

explanation.surface: Granny is impatient to get hold of some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing, China, so it is a kind of textile.

clue.text: Victoria's got plenty of these shoes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: London Victoria is a major railway station with many raised areas beside the tracks
second meaning: footwear with very thick soles

explanation.surface: Suggests Victoria Beckham, famed for her fashion, owns many pairs of a particular shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a big London railway station, not the fashion icon the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Stations have raised boarding areas beside the tracks, and thick-soled footwear carries the same name.

clue.text: Firstly pay rent, if you wouldn't mind

indicators.note: firstly points to the opening letter of the word that comes straight after it

parts.note: the opening letter of pay
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A landlord's polite request that the tenant settle the rent before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Please is the polite word attached to a request, meaning roughly the same as asking kindly for a favour.

clue.text: A copper nabs tense friend, in reality

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to nab is to catch and hold, so the policeman's letters close around the grammar letter

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests a nervous friend, and it really happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal, symbol Cu, which wraps around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually is an adverb meaning truly or as a matter of fact, the same sense as in reality.

clue.text: Female with thongs exposes flesh indecently

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a thong can be a leather strip used as a whip, or lash

explanation.surface: A woman in skimpy underwear is showing rather too much skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Thongs suggests skimpy underwear, but here it means whips.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who flashes briefly shows their naked body in public, which is an indecent act.

clue.text: Picture from US hospital department put up here

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means it reads from bottom to top, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: ER, the emergency room, is the American name for the casualty department
to be here is to be present

explanation.surface: An image from an American hospital ward is being hung up on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to depict it, and to represent something is likewise to portray it in art.

clue.text: Old boy comes out of lewd part of play

indicators.note: when something comes out of a word it leaves, so those letters are taken away from it

parts.note: obscene means lewd
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An elderly man walks out of a theatre during a rude bit of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OB from OBSCENE leaves SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is divided into acts and those into shorter sections, each one being a scene.

clue.text: Rook inside cuckoo nest's got most forceful

indicators.note: inside tells us the chess piece's letter sits within the other letters
cuckoo means crazy, so the following letters are scrambled into a mad order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird has taken over a cuckoo's nest and turned out to be the toughest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook and cuckoo both look like birds; one is a chess piece, the other an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongest is the superlative of strong, meaning having the greatest power or force.

clue.text: Enough beer swallowed by politician? On the contrary!

indicators.note: to be swallowed by something is to end up inside it; the exclamation that follows swaps which word holds which
on the contrary turns the stated roles round, so the politician goes inside the beer instead

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Asks whether a politician has downed sufficient beer, then flips the idea round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' reverses the instruction: the politician goes inside the beer, not the beer inside the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or more than sufficient, so it covers the sense of enough.

clue.text: Schoolhouse lesson somewhat inadequate

indicators.note: somewhat means only a portion, so just part of the adjoining text is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A rather poor lesson in a village school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless fails to do its job, so it is inadequate for its purpose.

clue.text: Carry off a Greek character and the first lady

parts.note: taken as written
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone abducts a Greek man together with the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The first lady sounds like a president's spouse; here it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry off a task is to pull it off successfully, which is to accomplish it.

clue.text: Saw a final bit of baccy in pipe

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word for pipe

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice

indicators.note: the final bit of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of baccy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone noticed the last scrap of tobacco left in a smoker's pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like a past tense verb; it is a noun meaning an old maxim. Baccy is British slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, and a saying is a well-known phrase of the same kind.

clue.text: Kid's expression of hesitation after toy gun's broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the toy are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A child hesitates once their toy gun is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid's stands for kid is, the definition plus a joining verb; after places ER at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, and a kid is an informal word for a child.

clue.text: US general's captivating student groups

indicators.note: to captivate is literally to take captive, so the general's name holds the learner's letter prisoner

parts.note: George Custer was a US cavalry general, here with the possessive S
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: An American general is charming groups of students.
explanation.walkthrough: Captivating suggests charm; here it means holding captive.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusters are bunches of things gathered close together, so they are groups.

clue.text: Hand over type of plaster after certain cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word for certain loses its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
render is a coat of plaster applied to walls

explanation.surface: Instructions to pass across a kind of plaster after a sure cut has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: After puts the shortened word for certain before RENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender something is to give it up or yield it to another, so it means hand over.

clue.text: Conservative guarantees reprimands

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A Tory politician makes sure there will be telling-offs.
explanation.definitionFit: Censures are formal expressions of strong disapproval, the same as official rebukes or reprimands.

clue.text: Relative upset the guard

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member has annoyed the sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child of her parents, and so a family relation.

clue.text: Hold bra up after husband starts to obstruct underwear refund

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom upward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so each following word gives its initial

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A lingerie return gone wrong, with a husband in the way of the refund.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the husband's H before the reversed bra and the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a feeling or a fugitive is to keep or shelter it, which is to hold it.

clue.text: Of higher quality, I'll wager

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the comparative of good

definitions.note: a description of the person who says it, a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who says this is a gambler, one who places bets

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is said by the answer: a person who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Better is the comparative of good, and also names someone who stakes money on outcomes.

clue.text: Radical old setter hosts Tories occasionally

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the setter's letters enclose the letters picked out next

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters of the word are used

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A former crossword compiler with extreme views entertains some Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Old and setter together make the host, and the picked letters sit between its two halves; the setter is the 'me' of the clue writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical position goes far beyond the mainstream, so it is extreme in its views.

clue.text: Pines for girls

definitions.meaning: first meaning: longs for someone absent
second meaning: young women, as in the title Miss

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one lovesick sentence; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss someone is to long for them, and young unmarried women are addressed with the title Miss.

clue.text: Works out good uniform is hidden in sacks

indicators.note: something hidden in is tucked inside, so those letters sit within the word for sacks

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
G for good and U for uniform in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a decent uniform has been stashed in bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Sacks looks like bags; here it is the verb to dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure something out is to calculate or deduce it, which is the same as working it out.

clue.text: Beats from loud records

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
logs are written records

explanation.surface: Suggests musical rhythms taken from noisy vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: Beats sounds musical alongside loud and records; here it is the verb to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to whip or thrash them, which is to beat them.

clue.text: Passionate, popular and perfect?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the perfect is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone fervent, well liked and flawless is the ideal person.
explanation.walkthrough: Perfect looks like an adjective of praise; it is the name of a verb tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and deeply felt, which is what passionate describes.

clue.text: Famous school raised doubts initially

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted to read from bottom to top, so the school name runs backwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of doubts

explanation.surface: A well-known school has expressed some early misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is well known and distinguished, the same sense as being renowned.

clue.text: Trump dismissed party

parts.note: a batter who is dismissed in cricket is out
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Reads like a headline that Donald Trump has thrown out a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump looks like the politician; it is the verb meaning to beat. A do is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump a rival is to surpass or beat them, which is exactly what outdoing them means.

clue.text: Dodgy dates with creep no adult's appreciated

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shifty, so the letters are rearranged
no adult means without the letter for adult, so it is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for adult; the removed letter

explanation.surface: Suspicious romantic outings with a sleazy man, no grown-up present, are welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A from DATES and CREEP, then rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone respected is held in high regard, which is to be valued or appreciated.

clue.text: Shocks Parisian on piano with pay increases

parts.note: sur is French for on
p is the musical direction for soft, piano
a rise is a British word for a pay increase

explanation.surface: A French pianist is startled by a salary bump.
explanation.walkthrough: Parisian tells us to use the French word for on; a rise is British for a raise in salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprises are unexpected events that startle people, which is what shocks are.

clue.text: Cherry that is thrown back — duck!

indicators.note: thrown back means turned to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A warning shout to duck as a cherry is thrown back.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and exclamation make duck look like an order to dodge; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck whose down is used to fill quilts.
